summary: The reveal-state slice is correctly wired as discovery-only, but it needed hardening so packets are not overread as barriers and common reveal/hidden-content cases are less likely to be missed.

findings.remediation: Reveal-state findings and fixture prompt mappings now use 1.3.1/2.4.3/2.4.10/4.1.2; prompt packets preserve relatedScs for all four SCs.

findings.risk: Discovery packets could be overread as barriers
findings.remediation: The reveal-state LLM procedure now instructs judges to return UNCERTAIN from reveal discovery alone, and the deterministic packet-pressure scripts expect UNCERTAIN_DISCOVERY rather than LIKELY_BARRIER.
probeRevealStates now emits stable nth-of-type CSS paths for no-id controls; an adversarial two-button test verifies the second button is clicked.

findings.risk: False positives from text-only diffs and closed details visibility
findings.remediation: The reveal diff now requires newly visible nodes rather than text changes on already-visible nodes, and visibility respects closed details semantics.

findings.risk: False negatives for common reveal controls
findings.remediation: The discovery selector now includes popover, aria-haspopup, and data-reveal controls in addition to explicit aria-controls/details/tab patterns. Broader keyboard-only, shadow DOM, iframe, long-delay, and state-combination exploration remains deferred.
Visual capture now includes all 10 positive and all 10 negative reveal-state generated fixtures.

remainingLimitations: The lane still discovers revealed states rather than emitting dynamicSubjects into the v3 obligation ledger.
It does not yet rerun focus order, heading/structure, or name/role/value checks inside every revealed state.
Keyboard-only reveals, hover/focus reveals, long transitions, shadow DOM, same-origin iframes, and bounded state-combination exploration remain future work.
Discovery absence must not be interpreted as a pass.
